brief: For North Macedonia, the English-language external layer is unusually strong and highly structured: IFIs and EU bodies (IMF Article IV/PLL, EC enlargement reports, World Bank WBRER, EBRD transition assessments, EIB CESEE Bank Lending Survey, EBA equivalence annexes) supply dated, comparable, freely reusable assessments of the banking system and of payments integration, while BIS archives English translations of NBRNM governor speeches. The commercial layer splits into open-ish regional wires (SeeNews is the workhorse for MK bank earnings, rate decisions and M&A; bne IntelliNews adds analysis; BIRN adds investigations) and gated rating-agency output (Fitch BB+, S&P BB-/B), where the Ministry of Finance's own mirrors are the practical free substitute. A distinct and underexploited channel is foreign parent-group investor relations — NLB Group and ProCredit Holding publish audited English segment data on their MK banks that is more granular and timelier than most local disclosure. The main weaknesses are payments-specific international coverage, parent-group channels beyond NLB/ProCredit, and back-file access to paywalled wires; this cell contributes essentially no Macedonian-language coverage, which is confirmed as cell 13's job.
